steps.path: The Usage window and Settings → Assistant settings → Cloud providers
steps.headline: This is what done means for usage statistics.

rows.statement: Clicking a usage or cost chip opens the Usage window instead of a website.
The Usage window shows one account at a time, with tabs to pick the account.
Under an account's limit bars, one timeline shows how full the 7-day limit was and tokens used per day.
Each model's share of usage is listed under the charts.
The 24 hours range pairs tokens per hour with the 5-hour limit; 2 weeks and 3 months use the 7-day limit.
ChatGPT's tab adds its per-model limit and extra credits under the plan bars, only when ChatGPT reports them.
OpenRouter's tab shows credit left, dollars spent per day and each model's cost, with no limit line.
The same Usage view sits at the bottom of Cloud providers and matches the window's numbers.
Usage lives both in the chip window and inside Cloud providers in Settings.
rows.note: i think it should both be integrated in the cloud providers page somehow but then also shown when a user clicks the usage/cost chips in the status bar. currently these link out directly to provider pages, but that should now be an action in this popup/menu.

rows.statement: Usage can be seen by day.
Usage can be seen by provider.
Usage can be seen by model.
Usage is shown as both tokens and percentage of plan or cost.
rows.note: both tokens and percentage of plan/cost.

rows.statement: Claude Code sessions are counted in the same view as their own provider.
Plan usage shows limit bars plus shares, and also a dollar equivalent labelled as an estimate.
The OpenRouter card shows credit left once the key works, refreshed every few minutes and after each reply.
The ChatGPT card shows per-model limit and extra credits under the plan bars, only when reported.
The existing chip colours are the only low-limit warning; no new gear dot or notice appears.
Daily usage totals are kept for 90 days on your computer.
